log_rows.asr_text: But listen before you call me a coward. A breeze lifted her veil and I wanted her. I promised him buried treasure, led him into the thicket, and tied him to the cedar. She fought with her dagger, but I took her by force. Then she seized my arm. One of us must die, she said. She would go with the survivor, so I freed him. We fought fairly, sword against sword. Twenty-three strokes. No other man had lasted twenty. When he fell, she was gone. I took his weapons and left.

log_rows.asr_text: My wife said, Take me anywhere. Then she pointed at me. Kill that man. He pushed her away and asked me whether she should live or die. For that, I almost forgave him. But she fled. He cut one rope and left. I rose from the cedar and picked up the small dagger she had dropped. I stabbed myself in the chest. The thicket fell silent. Then someone crept towards me on soft feet, and unseen hand quietly drew the dagger from my chest. I sank forever into the darkness.

log_rows.asr_text: My wife said, Take me anywhere. Then she pointed at me. Kill that man. He pushed her away and asked me whether she should live or die. For that, I almost forgave him, but she fled. He cut one rope and left. I rose from the cedar and picked up the small dagger she had dropped. I stabbed myself in the chest. The thicket fell silent. Then someone crept towards me on soft feet.
